div.head: V Atr 14.1
div.ab: ⁊ to æghwylces apostoles heahtide fæste man ⁊ freolsige; buton to Philippus ⁊ Iacobus freolse ne beode wé nan fæsten for þam eastorlican freolse.
⁊ to æghwylces apostoles heahtide fæste man georne ⁊ freolsige; butan to Philippus ⁊ Iacobes freolse ne beode we nan fæsten for þam easterlican freolse.
⁊ to æghwilces apostoles heahtida fæste man ⁊ freolsige; butan to Philippus ⁊ Iacobus freolse ne beode we nan fæsten..
⁊ to æghwilces apostoles heahtida fæste man ⁊ freolsige; butan to Philippus ⁊ Iacobus freolse ne beode we nan fæsten [for þam eastorlican freolse].
And to æghwylces apostoles heahtide fæste man and freolsige; buton to Philippus and Iacobus freolse ne beode we nan fæsten for þam Eastorlican freolse.
Und zu jeden Apostels Festzeit faste und feiere man; nur zum Philippus- und Jacobus[-bi G2]-Feste [1. Mai] gebieten wir kein Fasten wegen des österlichen Festes.
And at the festival of every apostle let there be (eager, G2) fasting and feasting; only for the feast of Philip and James [1 May] we command no fast, because of the Easter festival.
And at the festival of every apostle there shall be fasting and festivity, except that at the festival of Philip and James we enjoin no fast [because of the Easter festival].
And at the festival of every Apostle there is to be fasting and festivity, except that we enjoin no fast for the festival of St Philip and St James, because of the Easter festival.
And for the feast of each apostle there is to be fasting and a holiday, but we order no fast for the Feasts of Philip and James because of Easter.
div.note: man and: man georne and G2
Feasts of Philip and James: The former is May 3, the latter April 30, though now more frequently celebrated on July 25.

laetabundum tempus ist die Zeit Ostern bis Himmelfahrt; Beda bei Piper 51
laetabundum tempus is the period from Easter to Ascension; Beda in Piper 51
In 1008 Easter fell on March 28th (see Nicolas, Chronology of History, Sec. Ed., p. 58).

note.label: festival
note.seg: It is rare that the feast of St Philip and St James (1 May) falls within the octave of Easter. In 1009 it fell within the fifteen days after Easter mentioned in chap. 18; but by “Easter festival” the whole period between Easter and Pentecost may be meant.
